title: Mu isamaa on minu arm
description: “My Fatherland Is My Love,” Gustav Ernesaks’s setting of a poem by Lydia Koidula. When the Soviets banned the national anthem, choirs and crowds at the song festival sang this instead, and they still close the festival with it.

title: Raua needmine
description: “Curse upon Iron,” a fierce choral piece by Veljo Tormis, built on old Finnic runic singing and a shaman drum. It was written as a protest against war and the machinery of the state.

title: Spiegel im Spiegel
description: “Mirror in the Mirror,” a slow, simple piece for piano and violin that Arvo Pärt wrote in Tallinn before he left the Soviet Union in 1980. He returned after independence, and his archive is in a forest west of the city.

title: Ei ole üksi ükski maa
description: “No Land Is Alone,” one of Alo Mattiisen’s Five Patriotic Songs, sung by huge crowds during the Singing Revolution in 1988, when Estonians gathered night after night at the song festival grounds.

title: Everybody
description: Estonia’s first Eurovision winner, sung by Tanel Padar and Dave Benton, a singer from Aruba who had settled in Tallinn. The win brought the 2002 contest to Tallinn, held in this arena.
